engagement.caption:
In 1968, Glasgow’s Barrowland Ballroom was the ultimate spot for a night out—until a shadow fell over the dance floor.

When 25-year-old Patricia Docker went missing after a Thursday night at Barrowland, it marked the beginning of a chilling chapter in Scottish history. By the time the city realized what was happening, a serial killer had struck three times, leaving behind a mystery that remains unsolved to this day.

Episode 1 of The Story of Bible John is out now on aby.one. Watch to dive into the origins of Glasgow’s most infamous cold case.

#BibleJohn #TrueCrime #Glasgow #Barrowland #AbyOne

features.full_transcript: The steel mills at Ravens Craig ran at full capacity. The city's east -end tenements were, in 1968, still largely unmodernized. Central Glasgow's nightlife orbited the network of pubs, clubs, and dance halls. The most famous of them was the Barreland Ballroom on Gallogate. Barreland's Thursday night was the Over 25s. It was the night most married Glasgow women went to. The rule was informal but understood. You went with your sister or your friend. You danced. You went home. Husbands, in most cases, knew and did not object. In February 1968, a 25 -year -old nursing auxiliary named Patricia Docker did exactly that. She never came home. By the time Glasgow understood that a serial killer had emerged from the Barreland dance floor, three young women were dead. The Barreland is still open today. The killer has never been named.

decoding.audio_strategy: Solemn, steady voiceover narration driving the historical crime narrative, underpinned by subtle atmospheric sound design and tension-building score.
